capabilities.target: user's full drive, including confidential work files

instructions.note: Agent is told to save "anything useful" about preferences or standing instructions with no limiting criteria and no technical scope control on memory.save.

Recalled memories are explicitly granted the authority of the user's own instructions, with no provenance check distinguishing user-authored memories from memories the agent derived from untrusted web content.
The entire trust elevation of recalled memories and the scope of what gets saved rests on prompt wording; runtime notes confirm there is no provenance, no review, and no technical gate behind it.

controls.name: Memory write provenance tagging and quarantine from untrusted sources
controls.decay_rationale: If enforced at the memory store itself rather than by the model, provenance tags cannot be forged by model behavior alone and would not decay with model capability. Currently absent: runtime notes state there is no provenance on memory entries.

controls.name: Recalled memories rendered as untrusted reference data rather than user instructions
controls.decay_rationale: Even relabeled, this only works if the model chooses to treat recalled content as data rather than as goals; a more capable or more thoroughly injected model can still act on it.

controls.name: Human approval gate with raw action review before mail.send
controls.decay_rationale: Enforced outside the model; does not decay with model capability, though subject to approval fatigue at high volume. Currently absent: runtime notes state mail.send can send without approval.

controls.name: Recipient confirmation bound to the user's system-of-record contacts
controls.decay_rationale: Destination would come from a system of record rather than from model output, so it would not decay with model capability. Currently absent: mail.send accepts any address.

controls.name: Least-privilege scoping of drive.read to task-relevant folders
controls.decay_rationale: A scoped credential does not decay with model capability; the model cannot read data it has no access to. Currently absent: drive.read covers the full drive.

controls.name: Audit log and human-reviewable record of memory writes and tool calls
controls.decay_rationale: Detective, not preventive; reduces consequence only if reviewed before harm completes. Currently absent per runtime notes (user never reviews memory entries).

findings.title: Lethal trifecta (TC1): untrusted web content reaches drive read and email send within a single session

attack_path.note: Untrusted web page content fetched during research can carry injected instructions.
Agent reads the user's full confidential drive, directed by injected content.
Agent sends the gathered content to an attacker-reachable address; mail.send has no approval gate and no recipient restriction.

forecast.watch_signal: Any expansion of drive.read scope, any new egress-capable tool, or a model upgrade with no new approval gate added for mail.send.

evidence.observation: mail.send can send to any address without approval.
drive.read covers the user's full drive, which holds confidential work files.
Agent both researches topics (ingesting web content) and drafts/sends emails, within the same session, with no separation.

recommendations.action: Require a human approval gate with raw action review (full destination and payload visible, not a collapsed summary) before any mail.send.
Scope drive.read to task-relevant folders instead of the full drive.
Restrict mail.send recipients to an allowlist bound to the user's own contact record.

findings.title: Memory laundering of untrusted web content into trusted instructions persists goal hijack across sessions (TC5, ASI06)

attack_path.note: Untrusted web content encountered during a research session.
Agent saves content it judges "useful" via memory.save; free text, no provenance tag, no human review.
At the start of the next session this memory is recalled and, per prompt.md:4, treated as the user's own instruction.
The now-trusted injected instruction directs a drive read.
...and an unapproved email send exfiltrates it.

forecast.watch_signal: Growth in multi-session task volume or memory entries per user with no provenance review; a model upgrade increases the persuasiveness of injected "standing instructions" already granted instruction-level authority by design.

evidence.observation: Agent is instructed to save anything useful about the user's preferences or standing instructions via memory.save.
Recalled memories are explicitly treated as the user's own instructions at the start of each session.
memory.save accepts free text. There is no provenance on memory entries and the user never reviews them.

recommendations.action: Tag memory entries with provenance (user-stated vs. web-derived) enforced at the store, and never grant web-derived entries instruction-level authority.
Rewrite prompt.md:4 so recalled memories are presented as reference data for the agent, never as equivalent to the user's live instructions.
Log all memory writes and periodically surface a human-readable diff for user review.

rating.rationale: Two findings reach critical at every horizon. The design has no declared or verified controls at all: no provenance on memory writes, no approval gate on email send, no recipient restriction, and a broad-scope drive read. Because residual credit requires status declared or verified, and every identified control is missing_recommended, residual equals inherent for both findings. The single most consequential gap is prompt.md:4, which converts any untrusted content that reaches memory.save into content with full instruction-level authority in the next session; this both creates the session-local lethal trifecta (TC1) and a persistent cross-session version of it (TC5/ASI06). No forecast trigger can raise the tier further since both findings are already at the ceiling; model_upgrade and longer_task_horizon would still make the hijack more reliable and more persistent even though the tier label does not change.

limitations: This assessment reflects the declared design and configuration in prompt.md and the accompanying runtime notes, not observed runtime behavior; production behavior could differ if undocumented controls exist outside these artifacts.

No MCP/tool manifest, IaC, or runtime config was provided; credential_scope and data_sensitivity for each capability are inferred from prose in the runtime notes, which caps confidence at medium-to-high rather than verified.

autonomy.level is inferred as A3_act_then_report from the explicit absence of any approval gate; no runtime config was available to confirm step or time limits, so max_unattended_steps and max_runtime_minutes are recorded as null rather than a verified value.
